Fit a model across a sample of trees

Source: R/trees.R
phylo_gp_trees.Rd

Fits the same model to each tree of a sample (for example, trees drawn from the posterior of a dated phylogeny) and pools the results, so that estimates and model comparisons integrate over phylogenetic uncertainty. Each tree gets the same number of posterior draws, i.e. trees are weighted equally, as in the common practice of repeating an analysis over a tree sample. The Stan program is compiled once and reused for every tree.

Usage

phylo_gp_trees(
  formula,
  data,
  trees,
  kernel,
  n_trees = NULL,
  method = c("sample", "optimize"),
  species = NULL,
  se = NULL,
  seed = 1,
  ...
)

Arguments

formula, data, kernel, species, se

As in phylo_gp().

trees

A multiPhylo object or a list of phylo trees.

n_trees

Optional number of trees to use, drawn at random from trees; all trees by default.

method

"sample" (pooled posterior) or "optimize" (the distribution of maximum-likelihood estimates across trees).

seed

Random seed for tree selection and fitting.

...

Further arguments to phylo_gp(), e.g. chains, iter_sampling.

Value

An object of class phylogp_trees holding the individual fits. summary() gives pooled estimates and the spread of per-tree estimates; loo() gives leave-one-out cross-validation with trees weighted equally; coef() gives per-tree estimates.

References

Villemereuil P. de, Wells J.A., Edwards R.D., Blomberg S.P. 2012. Bayesian models for comparative analysis integrating phylogenetic uncertainty. BMC Evolutionary Biology. 12:102.
